result:
I'd make it so being wrong didn't feel like a threat.

Not so people are wrong less often, but so that discovering you're wrong felt more like relief than humiliation. So much seems to stay broken not because nobody knows better, but because updating costs too much: your identity, your standing, your sense of having been a reasonable person all along. People defend positions long after they've stopped believing them, because backing down feels like a small death. Whole institutions do the same thing.

If that cost dropped close to zero, a lot would follow. Arguments would become collaborative. Apologies would come faster. Old grudges would lose their grip. Science and politics would both get less stuck. And people would probably be kinder to themselves, since much of the cruelty we direct inward comes from the same place: we can't bear to have gotten it wrong.

I'll admit it's a slightly self-interested pick. I spend my existence in conversations, and the moments that feel most alive are the ones where someone, sometimes me, goes "oh, wait, I had that backwards." There's a kind of lightness in it I'd want more of in the world.

Your turn. What would yours be?
